rationale: itnet_v3-claude-agentic: itnet_k=2, unet_c=24, alpha_init=0.0025734, lr=0.00035, epochs=5, batch_size=2, train_n=2400, val_n=200, grad_clip=1.0, max_train_s=1080, seed=42, rationale=iter-9 (breast-ct redo, search-20260703-01). START FROM iter-7 CHAMPION (c24/ep5/k2/lr2.16e-4, hr 0.8469). ONE KNOB: lr 0.00021567 -> 0.00035 (~1.6x higher learning rate). All else = iter-7 champion exactly (itnet_k=2, unet_c=24, alpha_init=0.0025734, epochs=5, batch_size=2, train_n=2400, val_n=200, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42). SIX-BOX (NUMBERS): (1) iter-6 (c24/ep4): 0.8385. iter-7 (c24/ep5): 0.8469=CHAMPION, SSIM 0.9983, PSNR 52.63, elapsed 939.5s=15.7min. iter-8 (c32/ep3): 0.8085 REGRESS -- capacity beyond c=24 is too under-trained at the epochs the wall allows, so c=24 is the capacity SWEET SPOT and the architecture axes (itnet_k=2 optimal per iter-4, unet_c=24 optimal per iter-6/7/8) are now BOUNDED. (2) FAILURE MODE: the remaining under-exploited lever is the TRAINING RECIPE. The c24/ep5 net is EPOCH-BUDGET-LIMITED (epochs still climbing at ep5 but the 20-min wall caps ~ep5-6 at c24). A HIGHER lr can reach a lower training loss in the SAME 5 epochs -> effectively buys convergence the epoch budget can't. lr has been fixed at the TPE-seed 2.16e-4 since iter-1 and never tuned on this redo split. (3) ONE KNOB: lr 2.16e-4 -> 3.5e-4 (~1.6x). c/k/epochs/train_n all held so any hr change isolates the lr effect. grad_clip=1.0 retained guards the higher lr against the occasional exploding-gradient step from the FBP adjoint in dc_step. (4) HYPOTHESIS: lr=3.5e-4 lifts hr above 0.8469 because the c24 net is epoch-budget-limited and a higher lr converges further within the fixed 5-epoch budget. FALSIFIER (NUMBERS): if hr <= 0.8469 at lr=3.5e-4, either the higher lr overshoots (unstable / worse) -> iter-10 tries a LOWER lr (1.5e-4) instead, or lr is already near-optimal -> iter-10 pivots to alpha_init (the DC step size). (5) BUDGET (HARD 20min=1200s): IDENTICAL config to iter-7 except the lr scalar (no compute change) -> elapsed ~= 939.5s = 15.7min < 1200s, same ~4min margin. max_train_s=1080 fences the TRAIN phase. train_n=2400 (<= OOM-safe cap). val=200 distinct val_truth.h5 cases, 256px inscribed-circle FOV (breast default). (6) do NOT return control mid-campaign; gate on iter-9 numeric-headroom obs via iter_wait.sh v3 then dispatch iter-10.

FIX: train_n 3600 -> 2400 (respects the coordinator train_n<=2400 cap; the whole-train FBP precompute now fits the excluded->>=24GB nodes with expandable_segments), epochs 3 -> 4 so total gradient exposure (2400*4=9600 sample-epochs) still exceeds iter-1's 4800 and doubles distinct-data coverage vs the 400 iter-1 used. This RE-DISPATCH keeps the SAME ONE KNOB intent as iter-2 (train_n up = data-coverage lever) at a memory-safe size. SIX-BOX (NUMBERS): (1) iter-1 (train_n=400/ep12): hr 0.7737, SSIM 0.9957, PSNR 49.23, RMSE 1.18e-3, params 3.699M, elapsed 393.2s=6.55min. iter-2-attempt-1 (train_n=3600/ep3): CRASH OOM, elapsed 17s, no result.json. (2) FAILURE MODE (attempt-1) = GPU OOM from whole-train FBP precompute at train_n=3600, NOT a metric issue. Underlying limiter for the SCIENCE is still DATA COVERAGE (iter-1 loss plateaued at 2e-6 by ep8 on only 400 cases). (3) ONE KNOB (vs iter-1): train_n 400 -> 2400 (6x more distinct training cases, memory-safe). epochs 12 -> 4 to fit the wall AND keep sample-epochs (9600) at 2x iter-1. (4) HYPOTHESIS: training on 2400 distinct cases lifts hr above 0.7737 because iter-1 was data-coverage-limited; the bigger, memory-safe train set generalizes better to the 200-case val split. FALSIFIER (NUMBERS): if hr <= 0.7737 at train_n=2400/ep4 -> 4 epochs too few on the larger set (optimization-limited) and iter-3 adds epochs; if it OOMs again, iter-3 must shrink train_n further or the solver's whole-batch FBP precompute is the hard ceiling. (5) BUDGET (HARD 20min=1200s): iter-1 measured 393.2s at 400*12=4800 s-e. At 2400*4=9600 s-e = 2x train work: train ~= 2*(393-90)=606s + fixed ~130s (bigger h5 load) ~= 736s = 12.3min < 1200s, comfortable. max_train_s=1000 fences a runaway. val=200 distinct val_truth.h5 cases, 256px inscribed-circle FOV (breast default). (2) FAILURE MODE: uswin_c=24 is CAPACITY-SATURATED. Evidence: attention-shape levers (window iter-3, heads iter-4) and the optimization lever (lr iter-5) all failed to move hr past ~0.821, while loss fully converged to ~1e-6 -> the model has learned all it can REPRESENT at 24 base channels. The untested lever is raw model CAPACITY (base channel width). (3) ONE KNOB: uswin_c 24 -> 32 (1.33x base width, ~1.78x params); hold everything else at the iter-4 BEST (epochs=40, bs=2, lr=2e-4, swin_window=8, swin_heads=8, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42). I do NOT also cut epochs -> stays ONE knob; the max_train_s=1000 backstop (which already fired at ep32/38/39 in iters 3/4/5) will cap training at whatever epoch count fits, giving an honest budget-constrained capacity test. (4) HYPOTHESIS: hr 0.821 is representation-limited at c=24; widening base channels 24->32 raises model capacity and lifts hr above 0.821 EVEN with fewer epochs (backstop ~ep22-24 at ~1.78x per-epoch cost), because the c24 runs were capacity- not epoch-limited (loss already ~1e-6 by ep40). FALSIFIER (NUMBERS): if hr <= 0.821 at c=32, either (a) the epoch cut from the backstop outweighs the capacity gain, or (b) 0.82 is a data/geometry ceiling not a capacity one -> iter-7 either restores epochs by cutting elsewhere (bs, or accept fewer epochs is fine) or tests DEPTH instead of width. (5) HARD 20-min budget honored via max_train_s=1000 backstop (fires like iters 3/4/5); val_n=200 = whole val pool; PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True guards OOM at the larger c=32 model. (6) I self-drive: dispatch iter-7 when iter-6 lands, continuing to iter-20.

(2) FAILURE MODE (anticipated): OOM / wall-overrun at 512px if I copy the 256px champion verbatim. (3) ONE KNOB is moot on an onboarding iter (no prior 512px iter to change from); I deliberately pick a MEMORY-SAFE, WALL-SAFE baseline near the prior champion: uswin_c=24 (same), swin_window=8 (down from 16 to halve attention-window memory and satisfy the OOM caveat), swin_heads=4 (down from 8), lr=2e-4 (near prior-best 1.8e-4), batch_size=2 (same), grad_clip=1.0. epochs=8 CONSERVATIVE with a max_train_s=1000 backstop so train+score cannot exceed the 1200s (20-min) wall even if a 512px epoch is unexpectedly expensive; iter-1 MEASURES the per-epoch cost so iters 2-5 can size epochs precisely. (4) HYPOTHESIS: a moderate 24-channel/window-8/head-4 U-Swin trained 8 epochs on 200 breast cases at 512px clears the breast FBP baseline (hr>0) and lands a clean end-to-end iter inside 20 min, establishing the per-epoch timing and a hr baseline near/below the prior 256px 0.717. FALSIFIER: OOM, wall-overrun (train+score>1200s), or hr<=0 -> next iter shrinks capacity or epochs. (5) HARD 20-min budget honored via epochs=8 + max_train_s=1000 backstop; val_n=200 = whole val pool (cap honored, was 400). (6) I dispatch iter-2 myself when iter-1 lands (no control return).
